correctness.rationale: The frozen proof uses genuine variable-step BDF2 with r_n=h_n/h_{n-1}, backward-Euler u1=u0/(1+x), and arbitrary positive alternating normalized steps x first, y second. Algebra gives det P=xy/(D_x D_y), trace P=[s²(2-s)+2xy(s+1)]/(D_x D_y), and discriminant s^4[(x-y)²-4(s-1)]/(D_x²D_y²). Independent SymPy expansion verifies this exact identity. For s<2 and Δ≥0, positive distinct eigenvalues and a positive dominant starter component or a positive Jordan correction at Δ=0 establish all-index positivity; complex roots oscillate in sign, and negative-real roots for s>2 force sign changes. The recurrence difference identity makes every positive trajectory strictly decreasing. Exact-rational 120-step trajectories corroborated both short-first (1/8,9/8) and long-first (9/8,1/8) boundary, and excluded equal-step example (3/5,3/5) displayed sign loss. The proof treats all index and parameter quantifiers; finite checks alone would not.

originality.rationale: The earlier October 26, 2026 full theorem Exact positivity threshold for alternating-grid BDF2 already proves the sharp boundary 0<λh≤2/(√r+1)² for a **long-first** H,h,H,h,... sequence with backward-Euler first step of size H. Algebra with r=H/h shows its boundary equals the submitted symmetric (x+y)² relation when x≥y. That whole long-first portion and its high-contrast limit are decisively prior and are NOT claimed novel. The earlier result does not cover the reverse **short-first** BE starter x<y, because changing time origin alters the initial BDF2 history. The submitted all-index argument covers this additional phase and proves the same sharp boundary/strict decay without inherited-starter equivalence. No checked stronger all-phases result was found; originality PASS best-of-knowledge for phase-completeness ONLY, with unusually large partial prior coverage and a residual possibility of trivial or implicit phase derivation in old Floquet analyses.
residual_risks: Substantial 2026-10-26 long-first prior theorem covers the exact same threshold and most of the submitted phase diagram; genuinely surviving novelty is short-first BE initialization/phase invariance only.

A general periodic fundamental-solution positivity theorem or implicit short-first corollary may erase the surviving increment; present assessment best-of-knowledge and no worldwide priority guarantee.

Importance resides in the nontrivial short-first starter analysis, not a claimed discovery of the already known boundary polynomial or high-contrast limit.
